sources.title: Extract is here: AI-powered planning data for every council in England
sources.verified_claim: MHCLG states Extract is live for all English LPAs and converts conservation-area, Article 4 and TPO documents into structured planning data. AI extraction improves accessibility but remains a data-production route, not exact candidate evidence without source and spatial validation.

sources.title: Transforming planning with PlanX and new funding to help local planning authorities reap the rewards
sources.verified_claim: MHCLG describes LPAs using open planning data and PlanX to improve application submission and back-office workflows. Digital service adoption does not establish a planning constraint or permission at any sample parcel.

sources.title: Data standards: Laying the groundwork for an open, faster, data-driven planning system
sources.verified_claim: MHCLG reports regulations requiring standardised plan timetable and housing-requirement data for authorities using the new plan-making system. Standardisation improves comparability but does not make every historic or local spatial dataset complete.

sources.title: Testing new planning data standards with industry: what we learned from phase 1 and where we go next
sources.verified_claim: MHCLG describes planning-application data standards as pilot and testing work with unresolved implementation questions moving into phase 2. Pilot status is retained and not treated as a universally implemented authoritative standard.

sources.title: Extract: unlocking England’s planning data
sources.verified_claim: MHCLG explains Extract converts scanned planning maps and documents into standardised geospatial data and notes the national platform already contains data from over 100 councils. Coverage is expanding and is not assumed complete for every candidate constraint.

sources.title: Prepare your data
sources.verified_claim: Planning Data lists supported datasets including Article 4 directions, brownfield land, conservation areas, developer contributions, listed buildings, plans and TPOs, while explicitly allowing data to improve over time. Platform presence is not proof of completeness.

sources.title: Documentation - Planning Data
sources.verified_claim: The official API documentation supports coordinate queries for intersecting planning constraints. Query capability alone is not evidence that the canonical candidate point was queried, hashed, cross-checked and bound in the required 330-result chain.

sources.title: Local Plan proposals map
sources.verified_claim: Enfield provides an interactive proposals map with GIS planning-policy data. An interactive map is a useful authoritative source route but no parcel_30762 policy intersection is inferred without exact canonical spatial matching.
